instruction: Two-room studio flat shell. Open `/opt/blender/blender` first; Bonsai is available inside it as the installed BIM extension. Open the provided /home/user/Desktop/init.ifc IFC4 model in Bonsai and use it as the starting project. The provided file is an editable metric IFC4 two-room studio flat shell with placeholder space names and an unfinished window set; inspect it in Bonsai/Blender, rename the spaces to the required room names and add the required window objects, then save the only required deliverable on the Desktop as /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc using Bonsai's IFC save/export controls. The final model must be a compact one-storey studio flat with a living area and a bathroom. The building should be a rectangular single-storey shell about 7 m by 4 m with walls about 3.0 m high and one floor slab. It must contain real IfcSpace objects named Living and Bath, at least 5 wall-like IfcWall or IfcWallStandardCase elements, at least 1 IfcSlab, at least 2 IfcDoor elements, and at least 2 IfcWindow elements. The deliverable must contain real IFC/BIM elements rather than ordinary Blender mesh placeholders or visual-only geometry. The exported IFC should use the IFC4 schema and have unique GlobalId values for IfcRoot objects. The shaped model should have an overall size roughly matching the shell, with X span about 7 m, Y span about 4 m, and Z span about 3.0 m. Other coordinates, wall thicknesses, opening positions, materials, object type names, relationship nesting, property sets, and harmless exporter metadata may vary as long as the saved IFC satisfies these requirements.
